text:
maria: Heads-up — Acme (dedicated us-west) reporting big throughput drop and intermittent 429s since ~09:10 UTC. Customer seeing high p99 latency + failed calls. I pulled runtime metrics and the continuous batcher is emitting a massive number of 1-2 token batches; queue depth is oscillating. Escalating here.

chong: Can you paste the alert / sample logs and the customer id? I can check scheduler traces.

maria: customer id: acct-AcmeCorp-42. Alert: "dedicated/throughput_drop" firing. Sample scheduler log excerpt:

```
2026-02-28T09:11:02Z INFO batcher:slot_start id=7 queue_depth=120 pending=118
2026-02-28T09:11:02Z DEBUG batcher:emit batch_size=1 tokens=16 latency_ms=3
2026-02-28T09:11:02Z DEBUG batcher:emit batch_size=1 tokens=8 latency_ms=2
2026-02-28T09:11:03Z WARN scheduler:backpressure thrash_count=18
2026-02-28T09:11:04Z INFO autoscale:decision no_scale_reasons=[\"low_util\"] gpu_util=14
```

Two things jump out: tiny batches despite queue_depth=120, and autoscaler refusing to scale (low_util reported). Also customer app saw 429 with body: `{\"error\":\"rate_limited\",\"reason\":\"throttled_by_scheduler\"}`

support-bot: Alert acked by support. Ticket #INC-1942 attached.

ryan: Tiny batches typically mean max_batch_tokens or min_batch_size interaction with continuous-batcher window. What's the model/token distribution? Are requests mostly short (1-10 tokens)?

maria: Yes — traffic is many short completions (chat-like), median tokens/request ~12. current config for this pool (excerpt):

```
{\"continuous_batcher\":{\"batch_window_ms\":5,\"max_batch_tokens\":512,\"min_batch_size\":1},\"scheduler\":{\"min_wait_ms\":2}}
```

chong: A 5ms window + min_batch_size=1 will often emit tiny batches when arrival jitter is high. Also max_batch_tokens 512 shouldn't stop small joins. But autoscaler showing low_util at 14% — that smells like the autoscale idle detector reading only RTF (runtime fraction) and ignoring queued work because our metric filter excludes pending queue tokens after the recent change. I filed a quick link: https://redwood.internal/ops/issue/1297

olga: Ok quick mitigation options: (1) increase batch_window_ms to 20-30ms for this pool to collect more requests, (2) set min_batch_size=4 temporarily, (3) route this customer to a higher concurrency nodepool (fallback). I can push a config change to the dedicated pool if you want.

maria: Can you try option (1) + (2) on a canary subset? This customer is production-critical. Also need repro steps to confirm.

ryan: Repro loop (short requests) — run this against the customer's dedicated endpoint: 

```
for i in seq 1 200; do
  curl -sS -X POST https://dedicated.us-west.redwood/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\",\"max_tokens\":8}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
```

That produces tiny batches locally in ~5-10s and you'll see batch_size distribution skewed to 1-2 in prometheus: `redwood_batcher_emitted_batch_size_bucket`

chong: I'm looking at scheduler traces now — there's a bug where the autoscale low_util check uses `gpu_busy_time / sample_window` but we recently switched to sampling only kernels_exec_time and not queue_wait_time. So when the gpu is busy but waiting on many tiny kernels, util appears low. This explains both tiny batches (fast kernels) and no autoscale. I'll open a hotfix.

olga: Pushed canary config to pool-acme-canary: batch_window_ms=25, min_batch_size=4. Deploy ID: deploy-921.

deploy-bot: deploy-921 started by olga — canary to pool-acme-canary (3 nodes)

maria: After canary apply — customer latency dropped p99 by ~45% and 429s stopped within 1 minute. Prometheus shows emitted batch sizes shifted: median batch_size from 1 -> 5.

chong: Confirmed autoscaler metric bug in prod — created PR #3589 to include queue_wait_time in the GPU busy calculation. If that merges we should see correct scale-ups for these workloads. Assigning to ryan for review.

ryan: Reviewing now. If merged, we'll roll in next patch window but prepare an emergency deploy if customer impact resumes.

maria: Next steps: olga to keep canary config for 2 hours, monitor cost impact; chong to land autoscale fix; ryan to review PR; postmortem after 24h with follow-up on better per-customer pooling and an option for adaptive batch_window.

olga: Can confirm canary metrics look stable — p99 down, no 429s. Keeping config for 1h then plan to roll to pool-acme-prod. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #INC-1942 updated: workaround applied (batcher window/min_batch_size), awaiting engineering fix.

maria: Thanks everyone. Please add any logs/links to the ticket. I'll ping account exec once we have the autoscale PR merged.

chong: Filing follow-up action items in #postmortems: autoscale-metric-fix, per-customer-batcher-presets, and better observability for tiny-batch spikes.

ryan: Noted. Will add a unit test to ensure queue_wait_time affects autoscale decisions.

maria: Closing here for now — will reopen if customer reports recurrence.
